title: Three in the Morning, Four at Night

source.book: Zhuangzi, On the Equality of Things
source.quote: The monkey keeper was handing out acorns. He said: 'Three in the morning, four at night.' The monkeys all flew into a rage. 'Then four in the morning and three at night,' he said, and the monkeys were all delighted. Nothing in name or reality was lost, yet joy and anger were put to use — that too is the way of things.

moral: The wording changed, but not one acorn was added — do not be talked around.
